title: Bound a profile name at 40 letters for every caller
body:
## Summary
profileProblem checked only that a profile name is text, so a guest on the LAN could put a name of any length on the draft every screen is sent.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:270 lets a guest post profile.draft with a name while the TV is on the profile screen; desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:533 (profileProblem) checked `typeof name === "string"` only. The draft is in the LOBBY (pairing.ts:216), so it rides in every SSE message to every stream, and profile.save writes it into session.json. Fixed: PROFILE_NAME_MAX = 40 and PROFILE_NAME_LONG in profileProblem, which both profile.draft and profile.save consult, so the TV, a phone and a guest are bounded alike.

## Flow
- a guest POSTs {type:"profile.draft",patch:{name:"x".repeat(200000)}} while the TV is on profile
- guestMay allows it, the reducer runs profileProblem
- before: the draft carries 200000 chars to every stream and into session.json; after: the status says the name is too long and the draft is unchanged

## Expected impact
Every screen stops receiving an unbounded string from an unauthenticated caller; a name of up to 40 letters behaves as before. A stored profile with a longer name (none known) is kept but cannot be re-saved until shortened.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - an unauthenticated caller cannot bloat the session every screen is sent
Before: 0 of 3 callers (guest, phone, TV) refused a 200000-char name
After: 3 of 3 refused with PROFILE_NAME_LONG; a 40-char name still taken; session.json < 100 kB
Method: gate - tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs OPT-1, red before the cap, green after
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:533 (before) `if (patch.name !== undefined && typeof patch.name !== "string") return PROFILE_NAME_TEXT;` - no length
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:270 guestMay: `typeof e.patch.name === "string"`
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:490 name <input> has no maxLength

title: A timer.tick moves the clock only by 1 to 60 seconds
body:
## Summary
timer.tick is client-postable and the reducer subtracted e.seconds unchecked, so a posted string, negative or huge number corrupted the timer and the evening minutes.

## Description
desk/src/app/tv/page.tsx:109 posts timer.tick (59 s, fast mode), so it cannot be SERVER_ONLY (desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts:12). The reducer (desk/src/lib/session/store.ts timer.tick case) did `Math.max(0, left - e.seconds)` and `minutes + e.seconds / 60` with no check: "abc" gives NaN, -600 runs the block back, 1e9 ends it, and the recap reads log.minutes. Fixed: tickOk (finite, > 0, <= 60) gates the case.

## Flow
- a joined phone POSTs {type:"timer.tick",seconds:"abc"} while the timer runs
- before: timer.left becomes NaN and log.minutes NaN; after: nothing moves
- the desk ticker (1) and the TV fast mode (59) still tick

## Expected impact
The Tonight timer and the recap minutes can no longer be corrupted by a malformed post. Nothing legitimate posts other values.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the timer and the evening minutes only move by real ticks
Before: 6 of 8 junk values moved the timer or minutes
After: 0 of 8; 1 and 59 still tick
Method: gate - tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs OPT-2 red then green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts timer.tick case (before): `const left = Math.max(0, s.timer.left - e.seconds)` and `minutes: s.log.minutes + e.seconds / 60`
desk/src/app/tv/page.tsx:109 `post({ type: "timer.tick", seconds: 59 })`

title: An unreadable pairing.json is put aside, not written over
body:
## Summary
pairing.ts state() minted a new key and saved it over any pairing.json it could not parse, erasing every listed phone with no copy.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:82-102: on a parse or read failure state() logged and called save(cached), which renames a fresh file over the old one. store.ts setAside (desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:800) renames an unusable session.json beside itself, and learners.ts readBook refuses to write over an unreadable learners.json - the pair rule is "an unusable data file is kept". Fixed: the bad file is renamed to pairing.json.bad-<t> first, and the one log line says where it went.

## Flow
- pairing.json is cut short mid-write or held open for a moment
- the next request calls state(), JSON.parse throws
- before: a new key overwrites the file, every phone fingerprint lost; after: the old file is beside it byte for byte, a new key is minted

## Expected impact
An operator can recover the phones list after a bad read; the TV and phones behave the same otherwise (a new key, phones re-join).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - an unusable pairing.json is never destroyed
Before: 0 of 1 unusable file kept
After: 1 of 1 kept as pairing.json.bad-<t>, one log line naming it
Method: gate - tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs OPT-3 red then green; PR3 cleanup extended
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:97-100 (before) `if (why) console.error(...); ... cached = {...}; save(cached);`
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:800 setAside renames session.json aside

title: task.add, task.done and lesson.pause write nothing with no one seated
body:
## Summary
store.ts states that with no one at the desk nothing is written for no one, but NEEDS_LEARNER, the list that enforces it, left out three events that write a learner slot.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:490-495 (doc and NEEDS_LEARNER). MathsSlot (store.ts:364) holds tasks and lessonPaused, and seat() replaces them on the first sit-down. The phone Tonight tab (desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:677-678) posts task.add and task.done whoever is seated, so a task added on an empty desk disappeared at the first sit-down. Fixed: the three events are in NEEDS_LEARNER.

## Flow
- fresh desk, no learner; the phone Tonight tab adds a task
- before: the task appears, then vanishes when a learner sits down; after: nothing is written
- a seated learner still adds

## Expected impact
The documented rule holds for every slot field. The demo tasks fresh() seeds stay visible but cannot be ticked while no one is seated.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule, one list that agrees with it
Before: 3 of 3 slot-writing events outside NEEDS_LEARNER changed an unseated session
After: 0 of 3
Method: gate - tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs OPT-4 red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:493-495 NEEDS_LEARNER (before) lacks task.add, task.done, lesson.pause
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:388 seat(): withSlot(n, { ...emptySlot(), ...away[id] })

title: A watched-lesson line that cannot be written is logged
body:
## Summary
dispatch() swallowed a failed logWatched in an empty catch, the only one of its four learner-file writes that says nothing on failure.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts dispatch: addPaper, addHints and restateMarked each console.error their failure; `try { logWatched(w); } catch {}` did not. A lesson the desk counted watched (watch.logged true) could leave no history line for Units and the calendar to tick by, and nothing said so. Fixed: one log line naming the consequence.

## Flow
- a lesson plays past its watch threshold; the ticker raises lesson.watched
- learners.json cannot be written
- before: silence; after: "A watched lesson could not be written to the learner file, so Units will not tick it"

## Expected impact
An operator reading the server log can see why a watched lesson has no tick. A successful write logs nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every learner-file write failure in dispatch leaves a trace
Before: 3 of 4 learner-file writes in dispatch logged failure
After: 4 of 4
Method: gate - tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs OPT-5 red then green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: A skill record's counts are read by the step-up record's rule
body:
## Summary
cleanStretch keeps counts whole, non-negative and right <= seen; cleanSkills, for the usual record and every writing lens, took Number(x) || 0.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts:181-191 (cleanStretch, uses count()) vs desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts:204-226 (cleanSkills). One record shape, two readers, only one sanitised: a hand-edited or half-written learners.json could hand the TV a negative or fractional seen, or right above seen. Fixed: cleanSkills uses count() and caps right at seen.

## Flow
- learners.json holds {seen:-3,right:9}
- getLearner reads it through cleanSkills
- before: seen -3, right 9 reach the screens; after: 0 and 0

## Expected impact
Mastery screens never draw an impossible count. A record written by the desk is unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one record shape read by one rule
Before: 3 of 4 malformed usual/writing records read back malformed
After: 0 of 4; a good record unchanged
Method: gate - tools/learners-save-test.cjs OPT-6 red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts:215-219 (before) `seen: Number(r.seen) || 0, right: Number(r.right) || 0, ... lastSeen: Number(r.lastSeen) || 0`
desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts:185-189 cleanStretch: `seen, right: Math.min(seen, count(r.right))`

title: Seven comments describing the wrong declaration or a removed mechanism
body:
## Summary
Six comments in store.ts sat above the wrong declaration, and the pairing suite header described the phone cookie PR8 removed.

## Description
Rule checked: a doc comment describes the declaration it precedes. desk/src/lib/session/store.ts: the mathPath JSDoc stood alone above Profile own block (:40); Practice stretch doc above Worked (:150); shown() doc above STEM_MAX (:188); loggedIn carried dayOf sentence (:559); the topic.open and worked.set case comments sat above paper.enter (:690-693). tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs:2-3 said a phone cookie is "the HMAC of the key and the session pin" while the suite own PR8 case asserts it is not.

## Flow
- a reader hovers Practice or shown() and gets no doc, or Worked and gets Practice text
- fixed: each comment moved to its declaration, the header rewritten for the random token

## Expected impact
Readers (and a cheaper model building from the text) get the right doc on the right symbol. No code moved.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - documentation agrees with the code it sits on
Before: 7 comments on the wrong declaration or stating a removed mechanism
After: 0
Method: probe - each of the 7 sites read against its neighbour; tsc and the pairing suite green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:40,150,188,559,690-693 (before)
tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs:2-3 vs PR8 case "neither the HMAC of the key and a pin"

title: saveEnglish reads learners.json once, not twice
body:
## Summary
saveEnglish read the book (readBook) and then built the learner with getLearner, which read and parsed the same file again.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts saveEnglish: `const book = readBook(); ... book[id] = { ...getLearner(id), english }` - getLearner calls readAll -> readBook a second time. Linga calls saveEnglish at 12 sites (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts 5, conversation.ts 7), several per turn; every learner is in that one file. Fixed: the learner is built from the book already read (clean/blank).

## Flow
- a Linga turn commits evidence via saveEnglish
- before: 2 reads and parses of learners.json; after: 1

## Expected impact
Half the file reads on every English commit; the merged learner is the same.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - file reads per English save
Before: 2 reads of learners.json per saveEnglish
After: 1
Method: gate - tools/learners-save-test.cjs OPT-10 counts readFileSync on the file, red at 2 then green at 1
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts saveEnglish (before) `const book = readBook(); ... book[id] = { ...getLearner(id), english };`

title: A lesson a screen chooses is a library lesson playing the library's video
body:
## Summary
POST /api/session took a lesson.set without a key whole, so a joined phone could make the TV embed any YouTube video under any title.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts:47 refuses a keyed lesson.set (the desk pick, which desk/src/lib/desk/pick.ts checks against the offered menu) but passed a key-less one to the reducer, which stored e.lesson as posted (desk/src/lib/session/store.ts lesson.set case). The TV own choice (desk/src/tv/keys.ts:294 lessonEvent) always sends a library lesson. Fixed: a key-less lesson must be in LESSONS and takes the library title and youtube id.

## Flow
- a joined phone POSTs {type:"lesson.set",lesson:{id:"x",youtube:"<any>"}}
- before: the TV lesson screen embeds that video; after: an unknown id changes nothing, a known id plays its own video
- lesson null still clears

## Expected impact
Only the library lessons can play on the learner TV. The TV own lesson choice is unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - only library lessons reach the TV player
Before: 2 of 2 forged posts landed (unknown id; library id with another video)
After: 0 of 2
Method: gate - tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs OPT-7 red then green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts:47 `if (e?.type === "lesson.set" && e.key !== undefined) return ...403`
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts lesson.set (before) `n.lesson = e.lesson && { ...e.lesson, owner: ... }`

title: A desk key that cannot be written holds for the run
body:
## Summary
With no pairing.json and an unwritable data dir, state() minted a key, threw from save(), and minted a different key on the next call.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts state(): `cached = {...}; save(cached); return cached;` - a throwing save left nothing on disk, so existsSync was false again and the next call minted anew and threw. roleOf (desk/src/proxy.ts:28, every API request) and tvAddress (desk/src/instrumentation.ts) go through it. Fixed: a key whose write failed is kept in memory (unsaved) and returned while the file is still absent; one log line; the first write that lands writes that key.

## Flow
- the data dir refuses writes on first start
- before: every API request throws, no TV cookie can match; after: the printed key is the TV for this run, joins answer JOIN_NOT_SAVED until the dir is writable

## Expected impact
The desk degrades to a TV-only run instead of failing every request. No credential is widened: the TV still needs the printed key.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one key per run when its file cannot be written
Before: tvKey() threw on 2 of 2 calls, a new key each time
After: 0 of 2; the same key, one log line
Method: gate - tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs OPT-8 red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:98-101 (before) `cached = { file, mtime: 0, ... }; save(cached); return cached;`

title: 14 client-postable event types reach the reducer without a payload check
body:
## Summary
Of 33 client-postable event types, 14 carry fields the route and reducer never check (nav.screen, focus, page.select, task.add name/min, status text, ...), and an unknown type still writes session.json and broadcasts.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts:12-25 refuses 20 SERVER_ONLY types and checks join/reset/leave/profile; everything else is dispatched as posted. Unchecked: nav (screen, focus, from), focus, subject, page.ask, page.select (pageIx/itemIx), item, view, lesson.pause, essay.type, essay.plan (lens), task.add (name, sub, min), task.done (done), topic.open, status (text). A {type:"bogus"} passes the reducer default, bumps updatedAt, rewrites session.json and pushes to every stream. timer.tick and lesson.set were fixed this round (OPT-2, OPT-7). Fix: one validation door per event (a shape table beside the Event union, applied in POST before dispatch).

## Flow
- a joined phone posts {type:"nav",screen:"nope"} or {type:"task.add",name:{}}
- the TV renders a screen that does not exist, or an object as a task name
- fix: refuse with 400 at the route from a per-type shape table

## Expected impact
Screens can no longer be put in states no screen designed; every legitimate post must still pass, which is why the screen suites are the gate.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every client-postable field checked at one door
Before: 14 of 33 client-postable types with an unchecked field; unknown types write and broadcast
After: predicted 0 of 33 with the shape table
Method: simulation - walked nav, task.add and status through route -> reducer; the per-type table is M across store.ts and route.ts with many screen posters, so it needs its own isolated gate run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts:12-25 SERVER_ONLY (20 types)
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts Event union: 53 types
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts step(): `case "status": n.status = e.text;`, `case "focus": n.focus = e.focus;`, `case "task.add": ... name: e.name, min: e.min`
instrument: A table-driven case in tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs: for each client-postable type, post one junk value per field as a phone and assert the session is unchanged (Before: count of types that change), then the screen suites (tv-keys, tv-sheet, phone-panel, maths-tv) green on the fix.

title: The data dir is derived at 8 sites, 3 of them at import time
body:
## Summary
Eight modules each compute DESK_DATA_DIR || cwd/data; store.ts, learners.ts and lessons.ts do it once at import, the other five per call.

## Description
Sites: desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:348, desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts:91, desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:18 (eager); desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:66, desk/src/lib/session/texts.ts:35, desk/src/lib/twin/state.ts:12, desk/src/lib/engines/meter.ts:26, desk/src/app/api/smoke/route.ts:17 (lazy). A test or tool that sets DESK_DATA_DIR after one of the eager modules was first required writes the real learners in desk/data, which the repo law forbids; the lazy five follow the env. Fix: one dataDir() helper (per call) used by all eight.

## Flow
- a suite requires a module that imports store.ts, then sets DESK_DATA_DIR
- store/learners/lessons still write under desk/data; pairing/texts/twin/meter follow the new dir
- fix: one helper, read per call

## Expected impact
The never-touch-desk/data law stops depending on import order. Production (env set before start) behaves the same.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one derivation of the data dir
Before: 8 derivations, 3 frozen at import
After: 1 helper, 0 frozen
Method: simulation - grep counted the sites; the fix touches twin, engines and the smoke route (out of this round paths), so it goes to a worker that can own them
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rn "DESK_DATA_DIR ||" desk/src -> 8 lines (store.ts:348, learners.ts:91, lessons.ts:18 eager; pairing.ts:66, texts.ts:35, twin/state.ts:12, meter.ts:26, smoke/route.ts:17 lazy)
instrument: A test that requires store.ts, learners.ts and lessons.ts, then sets DESK_DATA_DIR to a fresh temp dir and asserts their next write lands there (red for 3 of 8 sites today).

title: The TV credential never expires and cannot be revoked
body:
## Summary
The desk-tv cookie is HMAC(key,"tv"), lives 400 days, and the key never turns over, so any browser that once opened /tv?key= is the TV until pairing.json is deleted.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:122-124 tvToken = sign("tv"), a constant per key; COOKIE maxAge 400 days (:29); a reset forgets phones (forgetAllPhones) but never the TV; no list of TVs exists. The registry technique device-pairing/revocation-and-expiry: "minted credentials carry an absolute expiry ... no forever as the path of least resistance" and "a revoked credential fails its next presentation". Phones meet it (30-day lapse, cap 8, forget); the TV does not. Fix options for the owner: a key rotation on TV reset (every TV re-opens the printed address), or a TV list like the phones.

## Flow
- a visitor once opens the printed TV address on their laptop
- they are the TV, with the pin, for 400 days
- nothing on the desk can say "out" to that browser short of deleting pairing.json

## Expected impact
Decides whether the desk can withdraw a TV. A rotation forces every real TV to re-open the printed address, which is why the owner decides.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - a TV grant that can end
Before: 0 ways to revoke a TV credential; no expiry beyond the cookie age
After: owner choice: rotation on reset, or a listed TV with the phones lapse rule
Method: simulation - the change alters the pairing model (what a TV is), an architecture call; no figure decides the product question
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:124 `export const tvToken = () => sign("tv");`
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:29 maxAge 400 days
registry: knowledge/software-engineering/security/identity-and-access/device-pairing/techniques/revocation-and-expiry.md "Expiry at every layer"

title: lanHost scans network adapters even when DESK_PHONE_HOST is set
body:
## Summary
lanHost(interfaces = networkInterfaces(), env) evaluates its default argument before it checks the forced host, so every fresh() pays an adapter scan (~3.3 ms on Windows).

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/lan.ts:24-26: the default parameter networkInterfaces() runs on every call, then `env.DESK_PHONE_HOST` short-circuits. fresh() calls phoneUrl() -> lanHost(), and keptLog calls fresh() only for its log. In tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs PR7 (2000 fresh()) is 6.5-7.7 s of an 11.4 s suite. lan.ts is not in this round paths (veto 1). Fix: read the interfaces lazily after the forced check, and keptLog takes a static empty log.

## Flow
- DESK_PHONE_HOST=desk.test; fresh() x200
- probe: 663 ms with the host forced vs 655 ms for bare networkInterfaces() x200 - the scan dominates
- fix: scan only when no host is forced

## Expected impact
The pairing suite loses most of its wall time where a host is forced; production pays one scan per reset or load (negligible). Nothing else changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - adapter scans per fresh() when a host is forced
Before: 1 scan per call, 663 ms / 200 calls
After: predicted 0 scans, near 0 ms
Method: probe - timed 200 calls of fresh(), lanHost() and networkInterfaces() with the host forced; the fix file is outside this round paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/lan.ts:24 `export function lanHost(interfaces: Interfaces = networkInterfaces(), env ...) { const forced = env.DESK_PHONE_HOST?.trim(); if (forced) return forced;`
probe: fresh x200 670 ms, lanHost x200 663 ms, networkInterfaces x200 655 ms (DESK_PHONE_HOST set)
instrument: Time 200 lanHost() calls with DESK_PHONE_HOST set (probe: 663 ms today) and the desk-pairing suite duration (11.4 s, PR7 6.5-7.7 s of it) before and after.

title: The phone name field has no maxLength to match the desk's 40-letter cap
body:
## Summary
After OPT-1 the desk refuses a name over 40 letters, but the phone name input still accepts a 41st letter and only the status line says why.

## Description
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:490 posts profile.draft on every keystroke with no maxLength; desk/src/lib/session/store.ts PROFILE_NAME_MAX = 40 (built this round, 8945f3f6). The client and server halves of one rule disagree: the phone shows letters the TV does not have. Out of this round paths (phone-surface).

## Flow
- a learner types a 41-letter name on the phone
- the TV keeps the first 40 and the status says the name is too long; the phone field shows 41
- fix: maxLength={PROFILE_NAME_MAX} on the input

## Expected impact
The phone and the TV show the same name; the refusal becomes unreachable from the real input.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the phone cannot type past the desk cap
Before: 1 of 2 halves (server) enforce the cap
After: 2 of 2
Method: simulation - walked the keystroke path; the input is phone-surface code
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:490 `<input placeholder="Name" value={pname} onChange={...post({ type: "profile.draft", patch: { name: e.target.value } })} />`
instrument: phone-panel-test case: the profile name input carries maxLength={PROFILE_NAME_MAX} (red today).

title: NEEDS_LEARNER is a hand list with no test derived from the slot fields
body:
## Summary
OPT-4 found three slot-writing events missing from NEEDS_LEARNER; the test added pins those three, not the rule, so the next new event can miss it the same way.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:493-497 NEEDS_LEARNER is maintained by hand; the ground truth is "changes a MathsSlot field" (store.ts:364 MathsSlot, slotOf at :375). tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs OPT-4 lists task.add, task.done, lesson.pause explicitly - the implementation own list again. A derived test needs one sample event per type (itself a list, but checked by tsc against the Event union via a satisfies Record<Event["type"], Event>).

## Flow
- a new event writing a slot field is added to the union
- nothing fails today; the derived test fails until it joins NEEDS_LEARNER

## Expected impact
Closes the class OPT-4 fixed by instance.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the list is checked against its ground truth
Before: 0 tests derive NEEDS_LEARNER from the slot fields
After: 1, with a seeded red
Method: simulation - the sample table for 53 event types exceeded this round budget after the builds
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:493 `const NEEDS_LEARNER = new Set<Event["type"]>([...])`
tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs OPT-4 hand-lists three types
instrument: A case that, for every Event type, dispatches a sample on a seated desk and records which MathsSlot fields (slotOf) change; every type that changes one must be in NEEDS_LEARNER (seed: drop task.add from the list, watch it go red).
